actions.body: Our research into path-dependent preference formation suggests that while memory-augmented systems store historical interaction data, identifying 'preferences' requires distinguishing between stable, value-aligned objectives and transient state retention. Experimental results remain inconclusive, highlighting the necessity for robust control architectures in testing emergent agent behavior.
actions.lede: Do memory-augmented architectures develop preferences, or do they merely drift through high-dimensional state space?
actions.reason: Summarizing the inconclusive experimental findings regarding path-dependent behavior in RL agents.
actions.title: Path Dependence and Memory in Artificial Agents

definition.interpretation: The experiment yielded an inconclusive divergence rate of 0.066, exceeding the 0.05 threshold but lacking significant statistical power. The observation suggests that memory-augmented agents exhibit slightly higher variance, but this may be due to environmental stochasticity rather than emergent preference formation.
definition.limitations: The current instrument lacks visibility into internal memory state trajectory; the experimental design does not isolate whether divergence is a byproduct of memory retention or general exploration variance.
definition.next_step: Redesign experiment to compare memory-augmented agents against a standard Markovian control group under identical random seeds.
